source_text: Descending properties of morphisms in the fpqc topology

<STRUCT_0001>
In this section we find a large number of properties
of morphisms of algebraic spaces which are local on the base
in the fpqc topology. Please compare with
Descent, Section <REF_0001>
for the case of morphisms of schemes.

Let <MATH_0001> be a scheme.
The property <MATH_0002>``<MATH_0003> is quasi-compact''
is fpqc local on the base on algebraic spaces over <MATH_0004>.

We will use
Lemma <REF_0001>
to prove this. Assumptions (1) and (2) of that lemma follow from
Morphisms of Spaces,
Lemma <REF_0002>.
Let <MATH_0001> be a surjective flat morphism of affine schemes over <MATH_0002>.
Let <MATH_0003> be a morphism of algebraic spaces, and assume
that the base change <MATH_0004> is quasi-compact. We have
to show that <MATH_0005> is quasi-compact. To see this, using
Morphisms of Spaces,
Lemma <REF_0003>
again, it is enough to show that for every affine scheme <MATH_0006> and
morphism <MATH_0007> the fibre product <MATH_0008> is quasi-compact.
Here is a picture:

Note that all squares are cartesian and the bottom square consists
of affine schemes. The assumption that <MATH_0010> is quasi-compact combined with
the fact that <MATH_0011> is affine implies that
<MATH_0012> is quasi-compact. Since
<MATH_0013>
is surjective as a base change of <MATH_0014>
we conclude that <MATH_0015> is quasi-compact, see
Morphisms of Spaces,
Lemma <REF_0004>.
This finishes the proof.
